CORRECTED per QA's re-framing (M3.23-qa.json defect_2_workgroup_hole_dispatch_geometry_oob.attribution_determination) and FIXED in the blocker-fix pass (see the top-level `blocker_fix` section below) -- SUPERSEDES the original entry verbatim below, kept for record: the original framing ('DISCOVERED (same class)' as the genuinely pre-existing shared-memory/Lavapipe defect, 'not introduced by M3.23') OVERSTATED the pre-existing-ness. QA's correct characterization: the ENABLING CONDITIONS are genuinely pre-existing and untouched by this diff (HIR's placeholder-dims-for-HoleRef-workgroup behavior in axc-hir/src/lower.rs; axc-optimize's resolve_single_variant legacy-convention-only @workgroup resolution in enumerator.rs, zero diff lines), but the TRIGGERING CODE -- run_optimize's own dispatch-geometry invariant capture and its use in derive_workgroups -- is 100% NEW code written by this milestone (it could not have manifested before M3.23 since the old mock bench never dispatched anything). The correct framing is: 'a new consequence of new code faithfully implementing the r3 spec's own §1.4/§5 design, whose edge-case analysis under-predicted the failure mode' -- the spec's §5 text anticipated only under-coverage ('caught by the oracle, else NotChecked'), not the actual failure mode (OOB over-dispatch causing a crash on Lavapipe / silent wrong-output on NVIDIA). The pessimistic code reviewer independently reproduced this 3/3 as a BLOCKER (not a disclosable limitation) and required the fix before merge; §5 of the milestone spec has been corrected in place to describe the real failure mode. ORIGINAL (superseded) text: "DISCOVERED (same class): run_optimize's own dispatch-geometry invariant capture (per spec) reads the HIR's PLACEHOLDER [1,1,1] workgroup dims whenever @workgroup itself is a strategy hole (real dims aren't known until per-variant resolution). Combined with axc-optimize's resolve_single_variant only resolving @workgroup dims for the LEGACY 'workgroup_x'/'workgroup_y'/'workgroup_z' hole-naming convention (any other hole name silently leaves the compiled kernel's LocalSize at 1x1x1 for EVERY candidate -- a separate, pre-existing latent gap that happens to make AT-3014/AT-3016's inherited 'WG'/'BAD'-named fixtures accidentally safe), a workgroup_x-named hole causes a genuine, deterministic 32x-64x dispatch over-provisioning whose out-of-bounds buffer writes SIGSEGV Lavapipe (real NVIDIA's robustBufferAccess tolerates it). My new AT-3007/3008/3017/3017b fixtures work around this by bounding every buffer index via `i % N` (in-bounds by construction, verified stable across repeated runs on both platforms) rather than by touching axc-runtime or axc-optimize."

Both discoveries are recommended as follow-up bug reports against axc-runtime (shared-memory + resident-dispatch on Lavapipe) and axc-optimize (resolve_single_variant's @workgroup convention-name-only resolution, and run_optimize's placeholder-derived dispatch geometry for any hole-driven @workgroup) -- out of scope for M3.23 per its own 'Codegen/runtime/SPIR-V: UNCHANGED' mandate.

blocker_fix.trigger: M3.23-pessimistic-code-review.json the_ruling_defect_2: NEEDS_REVISION, BLOCKER. Independently reproduced 3/3 on the canonical `@strategy { workgroup_x: ?[32,64] }` autotune fixture via the shipped binary on Lavapipe: SIGSEGV / glibc heap-corruption abort, zero artifacts. Root cause: run_optimize's invariant-metadata capture read the HIR PLACEHOLDER `@workgroup` dims (`[1,1,1]`) whenever `@workgroup` itself is a `?hole`, then used that placeholder (via `derive_workgroups`) for EVERY variant's dispatch geometry, while the compiled SPIR-V's actual `LocalSize` was the RESOLVED value -- causing 32x-64x over-dispatch and out-of-bounds buffer writes (Lavapipe: crash; NVIDIA: silent OOB clamp / possibly-wrong winner).
blocker_fix.fix_summary: crates/axc-driver/src/optimize.rs only, no library/cross-crate changes. Added `local_size_from_spirv(words: &[u32]) -> Option<(u32,u32,u32)>` (~26 LOC incl. doc comment; ~15 LOC of actual scan logic): walks the SPIR-V instruction stream past the 5-word module header, finds `OpExecutionMode` (opcode 16) with mode `LocalSize` (17), and returns its 3 literal operands, returning `None` on a missing/malformed stream. Both `correctness_fn` and `bench_fn` closures now compute `let wg_dims = local_size_from_spirv(words).map(|(x,y,z)| [x,y,z]).unwrap_or(workgroup_size); let workgroups = bench_variant::derive_workgroups(&input_sizes, wg_dims, None);` PER VARIANT (using that variant's own compiled `words`) instead of reusing a single pre-captured `workgroups` value computed once (pre-substitution) from the placeholder. `workgroup_size` (the old invariant capture) is kept only as the fallback for literal-`@workgroup` kernels (no hole), where it is already correct and identical across all variants -- so literal-`@workgroup` kernel behavior is unchanged.
blocker_fix.loc_delta: optimize.rs: +96/-6 net (git diff --stat, local uncommitted). Within the reviewer's ~20-25 LOC estimate for the core fix; the remainder is doc comments explaining the blocker/root-cause/fix for future readers (consistent with this file's existing documentation density).
blocker_fix.cosmetic_fix_ordinal_numbering: DIVERGENCE-ORDINAL-NUMBERING (warnings, minor): VariantsDiverge's reported ordinals previously were the cfn-CALL-sequence counter, not the library's `variant.ordinal` -- diverging whenever an earlier variant fails resolve/codegen (grid_search `continue`s before calling cfn, so cfn's call-index skips ahead of the true ordinal). Fixed by building `cfn_call_to_true_ordinal: Vec<usize>` AFTER `grid_search` returns, by filtering `result.results` (which IS in true-ordinal order and covers every variant including resolve/codegen failures) for entries whose outcome is not a pre-correctness `resolve error:`/`codegen error:` `Failed(..)` -- exactly the variants for which `grid_search` actually invoked `cfn` -- then mapping each recorded call-index in `divergence` through this vector before constructing `OptimizeError::VariantsDiverge`. No library change; `BenchOutcome` added to the existing `use axc_optimize::grid_search::{...}` import list (already-public type, zero-diff to axc-optimize).
